drug_class: Combination cold and cough remedy (analgesic/antipyretic, cough suppressant, expectorant, antihistamine)
purpose: This combination medicine is used to relieve multiple symptoms of a cold or flu all at once, including fever, aches, cough, congestion, and runny nose. It is designed especially for nighttime use because one of the ingredients causes drowsiness, helping you rest while you recover. It does not cure your cold or flu — it just helps you feel more comfortable while your body heals.
how_it_works: Acetaminophen reduces fever and relieves pain and body aches. Dextromethorphan calms the part of your brain that triggers the urge to cough, so you cough less. Guaifenesin helps loosen and thin the mucus in your chest so it is easier to cough up, while Doxylamine is an antihistamine that dries up a runny nose and also makes you sleepy so you can rest.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness and dizziness are very common — this is expected, especially from the doxylamine. You may also notice dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, or an upset stomach. Some people feel a little lightheaded or have trouble urinating.
warnings: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine — combining alcohol with acetaminophen can seriously harm your liver. Do not take more than the recommended dose, and avoid taking other products that also contain acetaminophen at the same time, as too much can cause liver damage. Because this medicine causes drowsiness, do not drive or operate heavy machinery after taking it. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist first if you have liver disease, a breathing problem like asthma or COPD, an enlarged prostate, glaucoma, or if you take any antidepressants called MAOIs. This medicine is not recommended for children under 12 without a doctor's guidance.
typical_dosing: Adults and teenagers 12 years and older typically take one dose every 6 hours as needed, but no more than 4 doses in 24 hours. Always follow the directions on the package exactly. Since this is a nighttime formula, it is best taken right before bed. Do not take it for more than 7 days in a row unless your doctor tells you to.
